newsitem.title: SPAIN: Both digital, cable TV seen finding niche in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Both digital, cable TV seen finding niche in Spain.

text.p: Both digital satellite and cable television will find a niche in Spain's underdeveloped pay-TV market, after weeks of rancorous public debate, top Spanish telecoms experts said on Thursday.
"We believe that the two systems are going to co-exist and are going to need programming," Alejandro Echevarria, chairman of private channel Telecinco, told a telecoms conference.
The debate on the unlikely subject had escalated over the past several weeks into a name-calling match among telecoms executives, politicians and journalists.
But there seemed to be a consensus building in the industry.
"The development of pay TV will be a mixed system and not under one absolute controller," said Manuel Campo of commerical channel Antenna 3. "It's not going to serve to win or lose elections."

At heart are the lucrative broadcast rights for Spain's first and second division soccer league games, which were just sewn up in a deal between media holding company Sogecable, Antenna 3 and pay-television firm Canal Plus.

The deal gives a big boost to the digital satellite package Canalsatellite Digital, which is to be launched on January 30, and dampens prospects for a parallel platform being set up by Spanish telecoms operator Telefonica de Espana.
The Telefonica project, which is being joined by state owned Radio Television Espanola (RTVE), had counted on Antenna 3 and its soccer audience to make it fly.
